role: A gzip reader (RFC 1952 member header and trailer around an RFC 1951 inflater) that copies matches a word at a time (a distance-1 run is a memset): gunzip_file inflates a whole file into one buffer; gunzip_open/read/gets/close stream one through a 32 KiB window and a 4 MiB span, and fall back to zlib's gzread for a file they do not take. Gives the same bytes as zlib, checked against the trailer's CRC-32 (zlib's crc32) and length.
gpu: its former globals, function statics and lazily built tables are gone (lane/gpuenv, L2): per-environment state lives in struct env (csrc/engine/env.h), per-dimension state in the replay's dims, constant tables are built before main; csrc/tests/globals.sh lists what is left
functions gunzip_file, inflate_all, dynamic: heap buffers for the file, the output and the dynamic tables (load time, outside the tick)
function gunzip_file: file reads (I/O, load time only)
functions gunzip_open, produce: a heap window-plus-span buffer and the whole compressed file per stream (load time)
function crc_update: static crc_fold_ok, the CPU check at the first call; crc_fold uses x86 PCLMULQDQ intrinsics (target attribute), the GPU port needs the table CRC
notes: Ports no oracle/src file: it reads what java.util.zip.GZIPOutputStream writes (the snapshot's chunks.bin.gz and saved-chunks.bin.gz, through snapshot.c:load_chunk_bytes). Checked byte for byte against zlib's gzread on all 1474 .gz files under out/java (111 GB inflated; lane suitestart, 2026-09-25). The stream was checked the same way with random read sizes (identical on all 1474 files, 2.55x less time than gzread). The trailer CRC-32 folds 64-byte blocks with PCLMULQDQ (crc_fold, Gopal et al. 2009, the constants Chromium's zlib uses) where the CPU has it; checked against zlib's crc32 on 200,000 random buffers.
